question: Which native drag owner and UI policies should block dragging and drop indicators reuse?
trigger: The user accepted dnd as the next Best API Review ledger item. Assessment and research recording only; no product implementation or adoption authorized.
requirements: Move or copy exact selected blocks, disjoint selections and list descendants; preserve complete content and reachable named roots across valid schema and identity boundaries.
A refused one-editor transfer publishes no document or root mutation. Independent editors commit the target before source removal, without promising shared undo or a global transaction.

Copy never removes source content. Source removal requires private captured authority, current source-view permission and freshness covering the transferred root closure; external MIME data grants no deletion authority.
Canonical editor/root identity is distinct from mounted-view permission and lifetime. Equal public editor IDs, two views of one document, detach and replacement must remain correct.
Keep root-block, column and same-table-row placement policies distinct, with one neutral transfer owner. Retain stale-source degradation to copy unless the product law is deliberately changed.
Retain automatic copied-kit integration, custom media handles, inert mounted preview clones, offscreen selected payloads, exact ownerDocument cleanup and optional Upload admission.
Content-drag scrolling must choose the actual nested scrollport, continue while the pointer is stationary, refresh landing geometry after scrolling and stop on all terminal paths.

Reconcile historical review, execution, present source, runtime proof and adoption separately. Runtime replacement requires native and matched complete-drag scale proof with budgets fixed before measurement.
evidenceReuse: Inspected the March coverage proposal, April context guard, July package review, September kit lifetime/root-slot/UI extraction/preview work and Upload handoff. Retained their behavior laws and original proof limits; the recovered extraction outcome remains historical-unbound. Inspected eight distinct consumer families and eight audit units. Ran the current dnd-react partition (51 tests) and copied lifetime/Upload specs (6 tests). Two local real-model/Happy DOM probe files reproduce seven observations with backend or landing resolution mocked. They assert observed defects, not accepted behavior. Local ProseMirror, dropcursor and Tiptap files were inspected at pinned commits. Independent Architect and Interrogate reviewers inherited the lead session model; the challenge is same-family. Exact deployment model identity is unavailable.
summary: Pursue one Plite-owned drag transfer path and retire Plate's raw-element transfer, move and settlement protocol. Plate keeps block/list payload policy, column/table restrictions and copied presentation. Observed defects include colliding-root content substitution, copy becoming move in both paths, read-only-source deletion, duplication between two views of one document and Plite source deletion after refused insertion. Native bindings are the leading backend cut, but a React DnD gesture adapter sharing the same transfer owner remains credible if a distinct backend or application drag job earns it. DndPlugin survival, the exact hook contract, root-only freshness, native parity and scale stay design questions. Eight units reviewed, none excluded or without a disposition; two units retain existing selection/preview and Upload ownership. Next owner is one Task design plan for the coupled work.

reconciliation.question: Which native drag owner and UI policies should block dragging and drop indicators reuse?
reconciliation.reason: Retain package-owned drag preparation, every-member admission, mounted inert preview clones and the historical completion account. Reopen drag transfer and source settlement because current raw-element insertion loses root ownership and model/DOM probes contradict copy and permission laws. The recovered outcome stays historical-unbound; no adjacent UI result is superseded.

reconciliation.question: Which owner should reconcile browser input, IME, DOM mutations and document changes without competing write paths?
reconciliation.reason: Retain shared native-input arbitration and canonical transaction convergence. Repair the drag transfer handoff inside that ownership; do not replace the input kernel or reopen IME authority.

reconciliation.question: Which location guarantees survive edits, deletion, movement and root changes, and where do text, node and range targets need distinct contracts?
reconciliation.reason: Retain exact node-selection membership and distinct coordinate/range/anchor contracts. Drag should consume complete exact selections, not add a generic selection store or replace them with a bounding range.

reconciliation.question: Which mounted view owns widget and selection geometry, and can duplicate position stores or observers disappear?
reconciliation.reason: Retain exact mounted-view geometry and copied presentation. Drag previews and landing paint need that ownership; no duplicate global geometry or widget carrier is proposed.

reconciliation.question: What does transfer preserve across schemas and editor instances, and can one content-fitting owner replace feature-specific paste repair?
reconciliation.reason: Retain complete ContentSlice/root preservation and the canonical fitter. DnD bypasses that owner today; reopen its handoff only, without redesigning formats, projected clipboard or conversion.

reconciliation.question: Who owns an upload after a placeholder moves, disappears, is undone or outlives its editor, and can provider-specific state be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Retain Upload's dedicated draft lifecycle, atomic batch admission and root-aware placement. Normalize file input and decide absent/refused Upload fallback at drag transfer; do not add another file owner or inherit Upload completion as DnD proof.

alternatives: Keep or configure the two complete runtimes: reject as the lasting target. Local permission, copy and root fixes retain two payload/admission/settlement owners for the same neutral laws.

Change the Plate hooks to use one Plite transfer owner while retaining React DnD gestures: strongest alternative. It preserves supplied-manager composition and custom backend jobs, but must justify ongoing registrations, adapter state and public backend protocol.

Native Plite transfer with Plate policies and copied UI: leading target. It deletes the extra transport and raw backend contract for the observed jobs. Unchanged Plite lacks safe refusal/copy and exact node-drag authority, so this is a design direction, not accepted runtime.

Delete DndPlugin as well as the backend: compare folding its remaining policy and installation into existing owners. Retain a descriptor only for a demonstrated headless policy or automatic kit-installation capability. Show how plugin-backed slots still install; removal alone is incomplete.
Move all drag behavior to core or registry: reject. Core would absorb product list/table/column policy; copied components would duplicate neutral permission, payload and publication law.

Add a public drag-session object, backend framework, generic selected-key store, new package or pointer/keyboard framework: no current independent job justifies these additions. A pointer framework would still need the native external-content and file path.

Retain the current preview preparation and exact selection owners, plus Upload's dedicated lifecycle. Reuse Plite composed-scrollport geometry only after implementing and proving content-drag scrolling; its current caller extends mouse selection.
proofLimits: No product edits, full typecheck, trusted browser drag, physical device interaction, modifier negotiation, painted ghost/indicator proof or matched performance comparison. Existing browser suites were inspected but not run. The seven local observations use real editors under Happy DOM with mocked React DnD monitors/editor hooks or native landing-range resolution. Their probe files and logs are ignored local artifacts, whose hashes identify the observed bytes but do not make them available in a fresh checkout. The file wire-type and cross-editor column-guard findings are source-based. Primary-children-only freshness omits an explicit root-closure check; a root-only edit/deletion consequence needs runtime proof. Prior preview/browser and timing receipts remain dated. Global ledger validation has unrelated changing inventory inputs; recording this review does not certify the global inventory or any runtime adoption. Exact model identifier unavailable; Architect and Interrogate evidence is same-family.
